summary: The browser inference implementation has passed desktop Chromium tests, while physical Android, iPhone and Safari validation remains pending. Behavioural validity rests on public data only. New this round: home phone video (E20: the phone build finds the cat in 0.70 and the dog in 0.60 of frames; 14 % of dog frames show only a 'cat'), an independent audio test (E21: meow and bark pass the pre-set gate, purr and growl do not; only validated vocalization types are now shown or used as triggers in both engines), the first cat keypoint model (E24, research only), and the first detector trained here on CC BY images (G1, full 50k-image CPU run, 4.4 h): at its own operating point it finds far more pets on home video than the shipped detector (cat 0.81 vs 0.70, dog 0.86 vs 0.60 of frames), but it misses acceptance 1 on cat AP50 by 0.019, so the phone build keeps its detector for now.

evidence.ci: green on every push up to 2026-10-11; pushes of 2026-10-19 not yet observed from this workspace

key_results.g1_full_cpu_run: E4 full-curve AP50 cat 0.898 / dog 0.864 (M3 0.923 / 0.851); acceptance 1 with per-class operating points and its own verifier: cat 0.814 (needs 0.833), dog 0.749 (passes), specificity intervals overlap M3's; home video at the single tuning-selected point: cat frames 0.811, dog 0.856 vs phone build 0.697 / 0.598

decisions: The phone test build uses the licence-stated TF Hub detector. Q-M2 was answered on 2026-10-19: the MediaPipe Object Detector page states no licence for the weights, so the MediaPipe detector stays research-only. On home phone video (E20) the TF Hub detector is the better one anyway.

Only vocalization types that passed the pre-set FSD50K gate (meow, bark) are shown or open/support interpretations; unvalidated confident types (purr, growl, hiss) remain in the JSON and can only block an interpretation (E21).
The on-furniture relation ships as the pre-specified containment rule; the learned head was not better (E15 follow-up).
Dog keypoints, MammalNet-trained heads, the AwA-Pose cat keypoint heads and the bark-context model stay research-only (data terms).
Server analysis is opt-in; the default path never uploads media.
resources_needed: Run the phone test on one iPhone and one Android phone
Write access to an object-store prefix for training checkpoints (signed PUT URLs or a scoped service account; docs/DATA_TRANSFER_REQUEST.md section 6)
A Kaggle API token for CatFLW / DogFLW (cat and dog facial landmarks, research)
Annotators for G2 (70-100 h for 2,000 cats + 2,000 dogs), or a per-image licence check of the AwA2 cat and dog images used by E24
Household recordings: participants and a data controller (docs/household/CONSENT_AND_PRIVACY.md)
An HTTPS host with header control for the installed-app track (only after track A)
